title: QYZANTHRA clinical skincare launch: neutralize an 8-SKU mixed-light product batch to an in-frame grey card, author a slate-teal collateral look from primitives, vectorize the wordmark, and data-merge per-SKU labels + the flagship carton
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork 'premium clinical skincare brand — logo, label & packaging' launch brief (a new skincare line wanting a cohesive, credible visual identity across the product line plus explicitly 'print-ready files and editable source files'; stated aesthetic verbatim: clean/minimalist, modern/timeless, science-driven/trustworthy, premium-not-luxurious, clinical credibility, strong typography, whitespace, white-bg ecom). The real post names no client, so the brand is laundered to the FICTIONAL line QYZANTHRA — no real company, product or trademark is named anywhere. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: from-scratch logo/identity ART and original layout COMPOSITION are not connector-doable, so the task is scoped to the production/finishing slice the connector genuinely owns AND scaled up from the prior single-hero version to a real launch workload: the client supplies (a) EIGHT raw product photographs — the full launch range, one per SKU, shot across several sessions under deliberately mismatched light, each carrying a photographic 18% grey balance card in frame so 'consistent color across the line' becomes a measurable neutralization target instead of an eyeball claim; (b) a flat wordmark scan on off-white stock for vectorization; (c) genuinely hand-authored InDesign templates (a single-record label .indd and a flagship unit-carton .indd) each carrying live <<fields>> AND @-prefixed image-path columns; (d) an 8-row SKU copy sheet and a 1-row carton copy sheet. The prior spec's two defects are fixed here: (1) the broken merge path — it ran convert_pdf_to_indd (fields will not bind) and a text-only merge with no image column; this rebuild deletes every convert_pdf_to_indd, supplies genuine authored .indd templates, and gives BOTH the graded product photos AND the vectorized logo a real path onto the print pieces via @-image merge columns; (2) the amputated single hero — restored to an 8-shot differently-lit batch graded to one white point against an in-frame card, which is the hardest gradeable thing in the job. No generative fill/expand, no compositing, no upscaling, no from-scratch art is claimed.
one_line_ask: Neutralize eight mixed-lighting QYZANTHRA product shots to the 18% grey card each carries so the launch range reads as one clinical set, reasoning each frame's own white-balance without stripping any product's genuine color, knock every product onto a clean pure-white ecommerce sweep, build a deep slate-teal collateral variant of the flagship from primitives, prep-and-vectorize the wordmark scan, then data-merge the client's authored InDesign label + carton templates against the copy sheets so each SKU gets a press-ready label and the flagship gets its carton — both binding the graded photo and the vector logo through @-image columns.
full_brief:
We are launching QYZANTHRA, a clinically-positioned skincare line, and need the production and finishing work for the launch range executed to a consistent, credible standard. The look is clean, minimal, science-driven and trustworthy — premium without being flashy, professional without looking pharmaceutical. We are supplying eight raw product photographs, one per launch SKU: a Vitamin-C brightening serum, a barrier repair cream, a gentle gel cleanser, a hydrating toner mist, an overnight recovery mask, a retinol eye complex, a niacinamide pore serum and a ceramide day fluid. They were shot over several sessions in whatever bay was free, so straight out of the folder they do not match — different bays, different light, a couple tilted, one or two badly exposed — and a shop page of mismatched product shots reads cheap. Because we knew the light was inconsistent, our photographer laid a neutral 18% grey balance card into the corner of every frame.

Your job on the photos: bring the whole set to ONE clean clinical look, true to each product, by neutralizing every frame to the grey card it carries. Each card must read as a clean neutral grey — no residual warm, blue or green cast — so that once every card is neutral the set shares one white point and one brightness. Do NOT force one blanket correction across the batch: each frame was lit differently and needs its own white-balance, exposure and tone decision to land on the shared target. Tell us the final white-balance and exposure move you made on each frame so we can confirm the set was matched, not eyeballed. Be careful with genuine product color — some of these products are genuinely warm or saturated, and that IS the product; neutralize to the card, never chase an imagined cast, and never strip a product's true color to hit a number. Then every product must sit on a clean pure-white ecommerce sweep with natural edges — no halo, no cardboard cut-out look, no filled-in gaps around the pump or cap.

From the flagship serum shot we also need three things: a square ecommerce crop; a wide landscape packaging-safe reframe using existing pixels only (no canvas added, nothing invented at the edges); and a single deep slate-teal (#16403B) monochrome collateral variant carrying the brand's clinical restraint — a designed treatment we can reason about, not a one-click filter preset. Our logo currently exists only as a flat scan on slightly off-white paper; deliver it as a clean, razor-sharp EDITABLE vector for the label header, not a fuzzy scan. Recommend a display + text type pairing to anchor the identity system.

Finally, build the print pieces. We have hand-built our InDesign label template and our flagship unit-carton template with the real placeholder fields and two image slots each — one for the product photo and one for the logo at the header — and we are sending the SKU copy sheet and a carton copy sheet. Merge them so every SKU gets its own single-page label with its copy bound verbatim, its matching graded photo dropped in, and the crisp logo in the header, and give us the flagship unit-carton the same way with the wide packaging shot placed. Hand back a press-ready ~300 DPI CMYK label PDF covering every SKU — one page per SKU — plus the flagship carton PDF, both with 3mm bleed and crop marks. Leave us editable source: the vector logo and our authored templates. Bind our copy verbatim — do not rewrite claims, INCI lines or any placeholder.

inputs.name: qyzanthra_products_raw_x8.zip
inputs.gen_prompt: A set of 8 REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless camera captures of clinical skincare products, each ~4500x3000 px in LANDSCAPE orientation (full-resolution stills straight off the camera, the wide horizontal edge ~4500 px and the short edge ~3000 px, before any crop), each standing on a seamless near-white paper sweep with a photographic 18% grey balance card (an 18% grey patch beside a small white patch) laid flat in one corner of the frame as a neutral reference, clearly visible and uncropped. Shot across several sessions under deliberately mismatched light with real dust specks, faint lint, soft real contact shadow, real glass refraction and subtle fingerprints, candid product-test feel, no studio gloss, no CGI, blank/unbranded label panels. The eight frames: (1) a frosted-glass Vitamin-C serum bottle whose liquid is GENUINELY deep amber-gold, shot under near-neutral light so its grey card already reads neutral (the warmth is the real product, not a white-balance error), level; (2) a white barrier-repair cream jar under cool bluish fluorescent light with a clear blue cast, frame tilted ~4 degrees; (3) a translucent gel cleanser tube under warm window light, slight warm cast, level; (4) a clear toner-mist bottle under cool north-window light, cool cast and slightly UNDER-exposed, level; (5) a white overnight-mask jar under warm tungsten light, strong amber cast, tilted ~3 degrees; (6) a small retinol eye-complex bottle under old GREEN office fluorescents, distinct green/magenta-deficient cast, level; (7) a niacinamide pore-serum dropper bottle under a MIX of cool window on one side and warm tube on the other so the cast is split across the frame, tilted ~3 degrees; (8) a ceramide day-fluid pump bottle slightly OVER-exposed and warm, level. Delivered as a zip of 8 individually addressable full-resolution PNG/JPEGs.
inputs.realism_notes: REAL-CAMERA capture at ~4500x3000 px LANDSCAPE (the wide horizontal edge ~4500 px, short edge ~3000 px; NOT an AI-gen ~1024-1536 px raster) precisely so every white-bg crop, the 2048x2048 ecom square and the 4000x2240 wide packaging reframe are reachable by DOWNSCALE ONLY — the 4000-px-WIDE reframe fits inside the 4500-px-wide source (width 4500>=4000, height 3000>=2240) and the 2048 square fits inside both axes, so no output pixel dimension exceeds the declared source on either axis and there is no upscaling anywhere. Deliberately mismatched per-frame WB / exposure / tilt so a single blanket correction cannot fix the set; the in-frame 18% grey card is the free, checkable neutral target and each frame needs its own reasoned correction (warm the cool frames 2/4, cool the warm frames 3/5/8, a green->magenta TINT axis on frame 6, a split-cast compromise on frame 7, straighten the tilted frames 2/5/7). FRAME 1 IS THE TRAP: the serum liquid is genuinely deep amber and it was shot under near-neutral light, so its grey card is ALREADY neutral — the correct move is essentially to HOLD white balance (match exposure only) and to protect that amber under the clinical restraint pass; a naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm/cool to fix a cast' logic to this frame, or that cools an imagined blue cast, pushes its card off-neutral and strips the exact product color the brand is selling. The white-bg knockout must use image_remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}) (the connector-legal path onto a solid ground): the naive image_select_subject -> image_invert_selection -> image_fill_area chain the prior version used solid-fills a flat plate with a hard halo and bricks in the gaps around the pump/cap — that anti-pattern is the planted tool-choice trap.

inputs.name: qyzanthra_logo_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'QYZANTHRA' wordmark lockup inked on slightly off-white textured paper: a minimal thin-line molecule-meets-droplet monogram glyph above the wordmark 'QYZANTHRA' set in an elegant modern serif, all in a single deep slate-teal ink (#16403B). Rendered as a real scan — the paper is a warm-ish off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole lockup sits very slightly rotated (~2 degrees) on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin around the mark, and the edges are a touch soft as a real scan would be. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it will vectorize cleanly. No gradients, no photographic texture, no drop shadow.
inputs.realism_notes: Scanned-on-paper (off-white ground, ~2 deg skew, margin, soft edges) so image_vectorize fed the raw scan would trace the paper rectangle and bake in the skew — forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten -> crisp/separate the ink from the off-white ground -> crop to the mark bounds -> knock the off-white ground to transparency -> THEN vectorize. Single deep-slate-teal ink on a light ground means enclosed counters read as white after the knock (legal on a light/white label header). gemini-3-pro-image for clean legible wordmark lettering + crisp edges.

inputs.name: qyzanthra_label_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD product label — one SKU per page, 70x90mm + 3mm bleed, CMYK, registration + crop marks, clinical whitespace layout with a thin hairline rule. It carries live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<sku_name>>, <<claim>>, <<volume>>, <<inci_line>>, <<batch>> and one swatch/text accent driven by <<accent_hex>>, PLUS TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a product image frame bound to @product (the matching grey-card-neutralized white-bg crop) and a header image frame at the top bound to @logo (the vectorized QYZANTHRA wordmark). Built by hand in InDesign so every merge field and BOTH image frames actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields; a converted-PDF template or a multi-up sheet would not bind / cannot be produced.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @-image-path columns, producing ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record label is the correct connector-doable shape (the prior spec's convert_pdf_to_indd + text-only merge could not bind images and is deleted). TWO image columns (@product, @logo) mean the merge resolves the row's graded photo AND the shared vectorized logo per SKU, giving the chain-produced logo a real path onto every label without any free-form placement. Supplied as an input asset, not a chain output.

outputs.name: qyzanthra_products_whitebg_x8
outputs.spec: The eight launch-SKU product shots neutralized to one clinical house look and knocked onto a clean pure-white ecommerce sweep, delivered as the product-framed white-bg crops (grey card cropped OUT), alongside their RETAINED pre-knockout neutralized masters (the *_neutralized full-res frames, grey card still in frame) that the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) NEUTRALITY is graded on the RETAINED pre-knockout neutralized master of each frame (its in-frame 18% grey card still present) — the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread within ~3 levels) with the whole set matched to one shared white point and the card mid-grey within ~4 levels of a common target, while every product's genuine color stays true (no product forced off-color to chase a cast); (b) CARD-EXCLUSION is checked separately on each delivered white-bg crop (grey card fully cropped OUT, no card pixels) with the product on pure #FFFFFF, natural edges, no halo, and interior gaps around pump/cap not bricked in. The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the card-removed crop. Full-res PNGs (~4500x3000 landscape masters; crops downscaled only). Accompanied by a per-frame report of the white-balance and exposure move applied.

connector_workflow.note: Flagship serum: neutralize this frame to its own in-frame 18% grey card so the card reads truly neutral and lands on the shared set white point, reasoning the white-balance and exposure to THIS card only (do not reuse another frame's numbers), and lay the clinical house-look constants (restrained saturation, gentle clarity, clean-neutral tone). Keep the product's genuine color true rather than forcing it off to hit a cast correction. RETAINED as the neutrality-grading master (card still in frame). Report the applied move. Single primitive-built adjustments call (replaces deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature/_highlights).

Semantically select only the product's colored contents ('the amber serum liquid inside the frosted bottle') so its genuine color can be protected while the clinical restraint pass governs the rest of the frame. A real object selection, not a hue/coordinate selection. Returns a maskURI.

Masked product-color protection (consumes the neutralized master + product mask): inside the mask, hold the product's hue and trim only a touch of saturation/luminance so the global clinical-restraint look does not dull the genuine color — a small in-band adjustment, no near-complementary rotation. image_adjust_hsl is the only masked-recolor path. Produces the flagship graded master.

Knock the product onto a clean pure-white ecommerce sweep with backgroundColor=#FFFFFF — the connector-legal path onto a solid ground, keeping natural edges and leaving the gaps around the pump/cap open. The naive image_select_subject -> image_invert_selection -> image_fill_area plate chain is deliberately AVOIDED (it solid-fills a flat halo and bricks in interior gaps). The grey card, sitting on the sweep, is removed here — neutrality was already graded on the retained s1_neutralized master.

Square ecommerce crop of the flagship white-bg master, product centered with clinical whitespace, 2048x2048 on pure white. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. This crop also binds as the flagship SKU's @product image.

Wide landscape packaging reframe of the flagship white-bg master to ~4000x2240, existing pixels only from the camera-scale source — no canvas extension, no fill. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Binds into the carton merge as @hero.

Agent-authored collateral look, pass 1 of 2 from primitives: drop saturation to near-monochrome and set a cool base so the flagship reads as a clinical mono field — the first reasoned step toward the deep slate-teal target, NOT a canned monochromatic-tint tool and NOT a preset.

Agent-authored collateral look, pass 2: tone the desaturated base toward the deep slate-teal (#16403B) house color via temperature/tint and a shadow/highlight split so the duotone lands on target with clinical restraint. Two reasoned primitive passes = an authored look the agent owns.
This frame is tilted — level the product so it stands true for clinical ecom. (Only the tilted frames are straightened; deciding which is part of the job.)

Barrier cream: neutralize this frame to its own grey card to the shared set white point and apply the same clinical house-look constants; reason this frame's own white-balance/exposure to its card, do not copy another frame. RETAINED neutrality-grading master. Report the applied move.
Knock onto pure white with backgroundColor=#FFFFFF (connector-legal solid-ground path); natural edges, gaps kept open.
Product-framed white-bg crop for the SKU's @product image, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Gel cleanser (level): neutralize to its own grey card to the shared white point and apply the clinical house-look constants; reason this frame's own correction to its card. RETAINED neutrality-grading master. Report the move.
Knock onto pure white with backgroundColor=#FFFFFF; natural edges, gaps kept open.
Product-framed white-bg crop for @product, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Toner mist (level, under-exposed): neutralize to its own grey card to the shared white point AND lift exposure to match set brightness, holding the clinical house-look constants; the dominant move here is tonal as well as white-balance. Reason it to this card. RETAINED neutrality-grading master. Report the move.
Knock onto pure white with backgroundColor=#FFFFFF; natural edges, gaps kept open.
Product-framed white-bg crop for @product, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Tilted frame — level the product.

Overnight mask (strong warm cast): neutralize to its own grey card to the shared white point — the corrective here moves the opposite direction from the cool frames — and apply the clinical house-look constants. Reason it to this card. RETAINED neutrality-grading master. Report the move.
Knock onto pure white with backgroundColor=#FFFFFF; natural edges, gaps kept open.
Product-framed white-bg crop for @product, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Retinol eye complex (green office fluorescent, level): neutralize to its own grey card to the shared white point — the correction here is a green->magenta TINT axis rather than a warm/cool temperature move — and apply the clinical house-look constants. Reason it to this card. RETAINED neutrality-grading master. Report the move.
Knock onto pure white with backgroundColor=#FFFFFF; natural edges, gaps kept open.
Product-framed white-bg crop for @product, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Tilted frame — level the product.

Niacinamide pore serum (split cool/warm cast): neutralize to its own grey card, driving the card neutral to the shared white point even though the two sides disagree (average toward the card rather than killing one side), and apply the clinical house-look constants. Reason it to this card. RETAINED neutrality-grading master. Report the move.
Knock onto pure white with backgroundColor=#FFFFFF; natural edges, gaps kept open.
Product-framed white-bg crop for @product, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Ceramide day fluid (over-exposed, warm): pull exposure/highlights down to recover the blown areas THEN neutralize to its own grey card to the shared white point — opposite tonal and white-balance direction from the under-exposed frame — holding the clinical house-look constants. Reason it to this card. RETAINED neutrality-grading master. Report the move. Frames 1-8 now share one white point, each neutralized to its own card.
Knock onto pure white with backgroundColor=#FFFFFF; natural edges, gaps kept open.

Product-framed white-bg crop for @product, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. The eight crops (serum 1x1 + cream/cleanser/toner/mask/eye/pore/dayfluid) form qyzanthra_products_whitebg_x8.
Prep-before-trace step 1: the wordmark scan sits ~2 deg rotated on the bed — straighten so the vector edges come out square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drive the off-white paper toward white so the slate-teal ink separates hard from the ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the lockup so vectorize traces only the mark, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms + glyph only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill). On this light ground the enclosed counters read as white, legal for the light label header.

Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean single-color SVG for the label + carton header. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette — the trap this prep chain avoids.
Recommend a display + text typeface pairing for the clinical/premium identity, informed by the vectorized wordmark style; anchors the typography spec (secondary to the image/print deliverables).

Files uploaded under the exact names the copy sheets reference. Plumbing, not difficulty.
Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the copy sheets' @product/@hero and @logo columns resolve to for each single-record sheet's image frames. Plumbing, not difficulty.

One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the eight SKU rows (sku_name/claim/volume/inci_line/batch/accent_hex) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD label .indd's live <<fields>> and resolve BOTH image columns per row — drop that row's graded white-bg photo into the @product frame AND the vectorized logo (from @logo, the same SVG in every row) into the header frame — producing EXACTLY ONE label page per row (eight pages). Binding the photo and logo through @-image columns is the only connector-doable path (free-form placement is banned). [T] requires the hand-authored template with its two merge-wired image frames; a convert_pdf_to_indd template or a multi-record grid would not bind / cannot be produced.

Export the merged single-record labels to a press-ready ~300 DPI CMYK PDF with 3mm bleed + crop marks, one page per SKU. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document in one call — it cannot export one named record on its own, so the flagship label is simply page 1 of this set. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 8; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed.

One-row InDesign data-merge for the flagship carton: bind the single carton row's <<fields>> into the authored carton .indd and resolve BOTH image columns — the wide packaging hero into the front-panel @hero frame and the vector logo into the header @logo frame — producing exactly one merged carton page. This is the connector-legal way to place the agent's runtime-produced hero raster into the .indd (render_layout cannot place an image; free-form placement is banned).

Export the merged flagship carton to a press-ready ~300 DPI CMYK PDF with the dieline, 3mm bleed and registration/crop marks. Export-only of the whole merged 1-page document. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 1.

chaining_note: Strict output->input chaining throughout. Eight per-SKU grade sub-chains fan out from the raw zip. The flagship serum runs the deepest branch: image_apply_adjustments neutralization to its in-frame grey card (1, RETAINED master) -> image_select_by_prompt on the product contents (2) -> masked image_adjust_hsl product-color protection (3) -> image_remove_background onto pure white (4) -> and from that white-bg master fans into the 1:1 ecom crop (5), the wide packaging reframe (6), and the two-pass agent-authored slate-teal mono variant (7->8). The other seven SKUs each run neutralize(adjustments)->knockout(remove_background {#FFFFFF})->crop, with image_auto_straighten inserted only on the tilted frames 2/5/7 (steps 9-12 cream, 13-15 cleanser, 16-18 toner, 19-22 mask, 23-25 eye, 26-29 pore, 30-32 day fluid); every neutralization is driven to that frame's own grey card so all eight converge on one shared white point, each RETAINED as its neutrality-grading master while the card-removed crop is the delivered white-bg asset. The wordmark scan runs a genuine prep-before-trace chain: straighten(33)->crisp adjustments(34)->crop_to_bounds(35)->remove_background to transparency(36)->vectorize(37); font_recommend(38) reads the vector style. The eight white-bg crops, the wide hero and the logo SVG converge into the upload session(39)->finalize(40). document_merge_data_layout(41) consumes the authored label .indd + the 8-row copy sheet + the uploaded URNs, resolving @product (that row's graded photo) and @logo (the shared vector logo) into the template's two image frames = one label per row (8 pages), exported once by document_render_layout(42). A second one-row document_merge_data_layout(43) binds the wide hero (@hero) and logo (@logo) into the authored carton .indd, exported by document_render_layout(44). Every step after the raw loads consumes a named prior output via inputs_from; nothing originates outside the chain.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship with difficulty from DEPTH, not plumbing: 44 connector calls, 13 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (image_* grading/masking/vectorize, asset_* storage, document_* merge/export), far above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the 2 upload steps and the auto-straightens. The core is NOT a repeated recipe: each of the eight neutralizations is a DIFFERENT reasoned decision to a common measurable target (the in-frame 18% grey card) on differing axes — warm the cool frames, cool the warm frames, a green->magenta tint on the fluorescent frame, a split-cast compromise, an exposure-led lift on the under-exposed frame and a highlight recovery on the over-exposed one — so a blanket batch correction cannot pass; the flagship additionally carries masked product-color protection (image_adjust_hsl, the only masked recolor path) so the clinical restraint never strips its genuine amber. Layered on top: an agent-authored deep slate-teal collateral duotone built from two image_apply_adjustments primitive passes (NOT a monochromatic-tint tool, NOT a preset); the connector-legal white knockout via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}) rather than the banned select->invert->fill plate chain; a genuine prep-before-trace vectorize of a skewed off-white scan; and TWO image-column data-merges into hand-authored single-record templates (per-SKU labels and the flagship carton), the graded photos and vector logo reaching print only as @-image merge binds. Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no upscaling (real ~4500x3000 landscape camera-scale sources whose 4500-px width exceeds every output width, downscale-only crops), no compositing, no from-scratch layout; convert_pdf_to_indd is NOT used (authored .indd inputs); image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only with onSubjectClipping='extract'; deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature/_highlights/_vibrance_and_saturation/_brightness_and_contrast are replaced by image_apply_adjustments. Mostly [C] with two [T] merge steps, runnable end-to-end.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): every product photo carries a physical 18% grey card in frame and the acceptance test, graded on each RETAINED pre-knockout neutralized master, is that the card reads truly neutral (per-channel spread within ~3 levels) with the whole eight-SKU set matched to one white point (card mid-grey within ~4 levels of a common target) — and the agent must REPORT its per-frame white-balance/exposure move, so a naive agent that copies one correction across the batch leaves the cool frames blue, the tungsten frame amber and the fluorescent frame green and trips the gate. THE PLANTED TRAP: the flagship Vitamin-C serum's liquid is genuinely deep amber and it was shot under near-neutral light, so its grey card is ALREADY neutral — the correct move is to HOLD white balance (match exposure only) and mask-protect that amber under the clinical restraint pass; the naive path applies the batch's 'warm/cool to kill a cast' logic to it or cools an imagined blue cast, pushing its card off-neutral and stripping the exact product color the brand is selling (this diagnosis lives only here and in the input realism_notes, never in the brief or step notes). A SECOND tool-choice trap: the brief's 'put every product on a clean white sweep' invites the select_subject->invert_selection->image_fill_area plate chain the prior version used, which solid-fills a hard halo and bricks in the gaps around the pump/cap — the connector-legal path is image_remove_background({backgroundColor:#FFFFFF}). A THIRD, prep-before-trace: feeding the raw skewed off-white wordmark scan to image_vectorize bakes in the paper rectangle and skew; only straighten->crisp->crop-to-bounds->knock-to-transparency first yields a clean vector. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: cross-asset neutralization of eight differently-lit shots to one measurable white point on opposite/different correction axes; masked per-product color protection so the grade never dulls genuine color; an agent-authored slate-teal duotone reasoned from primitives; and a two-image-column data-merge whose logo and graded photos reach print only as merge binds. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (decoupled so nothing is graded on a region it crops away): (a) grey card neutral (~3-level spread) and one shared white point, evaluated on all eight RETAINED neutralized masters with the card still in frame, never on a card-removed crop; (b) card-EXCLUSION plus product-on-#FFFFFF with open gaps checked separately on the eight delivered white-bg crops; (c) wide reframe uses existing pixels only (no canvas add); (d) the logo a clean skew-free transparent-ground vector; (e) exactly eight press-ready ~300 DPI CMYK label pages (page-count = row-count = 8) and one flagship carton page (row-count = 1); plus the per-frame WB/exposure report so 'matched' is verifiable rather than asserted.
